correctness.rationale: For n≥2, gcd(n,k)=1 and P_{n,k}=(X^n−2X^k+1)/(X−1), reciprocal indices k and n−k give the same splitting field. The cited Garmi theorem supplies full S_(n−1) for n>8; the finite boundary is not inferred from numerical experiments. I independently reconstructed each P as the difference of the two consecutive coefficient blocks and used SymPy over exact rationals and finite fields to verify ten representative discriminants, irreducible Frobenius reductions, the (1,d−1) factor-cycle reductions in composite degrees d=4,6, and discriminant primes of valuation exactly one. The n=8 representatives (8,1),(8,3) have discriminants −5390272 and −1205696, irreducible modulo 7 and 3 respectively, and tame-transposition primes 84223 and 18839. Prime-degree transitivity gives primitivity, and a (d−1)-cycle with one fixed point forces primitivity for the composite d; a transposition then yields S_d. The exceptional n=7,k=2 factorization has two irreducible S3 cubics with discriminants −31 and −23, hence distinct quadratic subfields and linearly disjoint splitting fields, giving S3×S3. Edge cases n=2 and reciprocal k=5 are included. Thus the best uniform cutoff is N=8, conditional only on the precisely cited established n>8 theorem.

evidence: The strongest directly applicable earlier theorem is Garmi's n>8 uniform symmetric-Galois claim; it does not logically imply n=8. The general primitive-group/transposition criteria are classical tools, not a dominating parameter theorem; the two n=8 modular certificates remain necessary.

originality.rationale: The interesting new statement is the exact cutoff N=8 with explicit degree-seven Galois calculations; the large n>8 S_(n−1) theorem and the n=7 exceptional factorization are expressly prior. Garmi's public preprint specifies n>8 for the relevant coefficient-two family and a later public correction warns that n>8 matters to the corollary. Neither the checked indexed results nor the inspected abstract/correction covers the two endpoint n=8 polynomials. This is a best-of-knowledge assessment, not exhaustive priority certification: the Garmi full text was inaccessible during this run and older low-degree polynomial Galois tables could contain these exact entries.
residual_risks: Garmi full text and historical degree-seven Galois tables were not fully available; priority of the two n=8 certificates may predate this record.
No new general Galois theorem is proved beyond the external n>8 source; the result is confined to coprime exponents.

value.rationale: A least uniform threshold for full symmetric Galois groups across all coprime signed-block polynomials is a mathematically natural sharp boundary: the immediately preceding n=7 has two genuine exceptional S3×S3 splitting fields. Resolving both missing degree-seven cases, rather than merely citing a sufficient large-n theorem, closes a finite but structurally motivated gap. The calculation is a meaningful sharp cutoff, not a renamed restatement of the known infinite-range result.

limitations: Full uniform theorem relies on an external published result for n≥9; finite modular checks alone do not prove the infinite family.
